paper.title: Retroformer: Retrospective Large Language Agents with Policy Gradient Optimization
paper.central_claim: Retroformer trains a plug-in retrospective LM with policy gradient on return differences so that its reflections, appended to a frozen actor's prompt, make language agents improve faster across retries and outperform Reflexion-style baselines on HotPotQA, AlfWorld and WebShop.

provenance.notes: Opus aggregate seat via configured claude-kimi type fable; no route probing. actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are null because the subagent runtime exposes no verifiable provider receipt to this worker. Seat attempts used: sol a3, son55 a3 (input v3, text + page images).

gap.author_gap: 冻结 LLM 反思器难以做信用分配、给出可执行改进(Fig.1)，且现有语言 agent 的反思不能与基于梯度的奖励学习兼容。
gap.checked_gap: 核实后的具体瓶颈：Reflexion 类流程中'反思生成器'权重固定、无针对回报的训练。'与梯度学习兼容'属框架性措辞；具体可检验处是反思器质量(r=0/Reflexion vs 已训)。

assessment.evidence_level_note: The non-weight object (reflection text) persists only across retries of the same task with ground-truth feedback and is reset between tasks (as for Reflexion in cal-dev). What transfers to validation tasks is the reflector's weights, a component_training result, not a retained harness change.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With a frozen GPT-3/GPT-4 ReAct actor, ground-truth retry feedback and a single run, an offline SFT+RM+PPO LoRA-tuned 7B reflector raises within-task retry success over Reflexion clearly on AlfWorld (100% vs ~85%) and by 1-4 points on HotPotQA/WebShop, margins comparable to figure-table inconsistencies (author-reported).

G.reason: Concrete gap (frozen reflectors give uninformative reflections; no reward-driven learning of the reflector) with ReAct->Reflexion lineage; neighbour coverage narrow (no prompt optimisers).

M.reason: Actor-as-environment makes reflector training a standard RL problem; ΔG reward and RLHF pipeline are reconstructable; ΔG also absorbs trajectory chaos, and SFT/RM/PPO/best-of-n roles are not separated.

X.reason: Data collection -> SFT -> RM -> PPO -> best-of-n deployment is described with hyperparameters; n, the reflector used with GPT-4 and Algorithm 1's contradictory initialisation are unclear; no reflection gating or rollback.

E.measurement.reason: Environments have programmatic rewards, but 'success' is undefined for HotPotQA/WebShop (soft F1/attribute rewards), Fig. 4/6b disagree with Table 2 by ~1 point on the same configurations (the size of the HotPotQA/WebShop margins), and headline gains (18%/36%/4%) are not recomputable from Table 2.

E.causality.reason: ReAct, Reflexion and r=0 (untrained reflector, figure only) controls; no SFT/RM/PPO/best-of-n ablation and online best-of-n sampling not budget-matched.

E.holdout.reason: Train-split rollouts vs 100/134/100 validation tasks, but retries use ground-truth feedback on the evaluated task and checkpoint selection is unreported.

E.statistics.reason: Denominators and weak WebShop result reported; single run, no intervals or seeds (A2 ladder 1).

E.cost.reason: LoRA sizes, sample counts, A100 and hyperparameters only; no GPU-hours, API calls or best-of-n cost.
